text:
Priya: FYI escalation from AcmeHealth — they saw client requests flip between eu-central-1 and us-west-2 repeatedly and ~3k 5xxs in 15m. UX timeouts + massive token refresh churn. They're seeing billing jump.

Jordan: can you paste the timestamps/log snippets? region toggles every ~20s sounds like health-checks disagreeing.

Priya: paste from their logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-16T10:12:03Z request_id=abc region=eu-central-1 route=proxy_A status=200 latency_ms=45
2026-03-16T10:12:23Z request_id=abc region=us-west-2 route=proxy_B status=502 latency_ms=150
2026-03-16T10:12:43Z request_id=abc region=eu-central-1 route=proxy_A status=200 latency_ms=48
```
They also show auth token refresh errors: `401 refresh_failed` during switches.

Alex: ugh. Is this the lightweight probe (lightprobe) we rolled last week? That probe uses a short TCP check + header echo. If NAT mapping changes across regions we can misattribute health.

Sophie: Observability shows simultaneous health-check pass in both regions for the same customer CID (client IP) for ~2 minutes then rapid alternating failures. Metrics: probe_success_rate drops in each region ~0.92 -> 0.6 during window.

Priya: Customer says they have CPE NAT in front of their fleet and use ephemeral client source ports. Could be asymmetric path.

Jordan: Hypothesis: our router uses client IP + port hash to pick local endpoint; when NAT mapping rotates, the health probe (originating from load-balancer egress) hits different backend that thinks the client is new -> KV cache miss -> auth refresh -> 401 -> client retries -> routed to other region. Repeat.

Maria: Customer context: heavy traffic from a mobile app. They hit our hosted API with embedded region preference header `X-RW-Client-Region: eu` (but not enforced). They expect sticky routing.

Oncall Bot: Incident created INC-2026-21312 — high-psp-failover. Pager sent to eng-sre. :rotating_light:

Jordan: Quick repro we ran from office:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Region-Hint: eu-central-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
If we flip NAT on our test box (simulate ephemeral port change) we observed the same quick region switch and a 401 on the second request.

Alex: Mitigation options:
- Short term: enforce region pinning in our router for session TTL=300s when client includes region hint.
- Medium: make probe origin consistent (use persistent control-plane IP) so health-check source IP doesn't change across paths.
- Long term: bind session affinity to an application-level token (session cookie) not source IP.

Priya: Customer is asking for immediate relief. Can we enable region pin TTL=300s for their account?

Jordan: I can do a canary rule for the customer id (acct: acme-health) in routing-policy to set affinity TTL=300s. Will roll to 10% then 100% if green.

Maria: Customer approved canary. They want steps and ETA.

Jordan: ETA: 10m to stage rule to canary, monitor for 15m. If no regressions, push. I will add a temporary routing-exempt that ignores probe toggles for this account.

Sophie: Observability note: add dashboard panel comparing `probe_src_ip` vs `selected_region` for this account to confirm.

Priya: Thanks. Also please record repro steps for Support KB. I'll send customer a note: we are enabling temporary region affinity and monitoring.

Alex: After canary, we should audit the lightprobe config: increase probe TTL, or add an application-level health endpoint that validates token handshake before marking healthy.

deploy-bot: canary-rollout started: routing-policy/acme-health-affinity-ttl -> 10% (by policy id rp-9981).

Jordan: rolling now. I'll post results.

(15m later)

Jordan: Canary looks good — no further 401s and region oscillation stopped for the sampled traffic. Metrics: probe_toggle_rate down 95% for acct acme-health.

Priya: Customer confirmed UX recovered and billing spike abated. They asked for postmortem and a permanent fix.

Sophie: Action items: 1) postmortem + RCA, 2) change lightprobe origin to fixed IPs, 3) routing affinity improvements (session token), 4) KB update for support.

Maria: I'll notify customer and draft the PM.

Jordan: Logging follow-up: add a correlation id at router when routing decision flips so we can trace per-request region handoffs.

Priya: Closing loop here. Thanks team. :heart:
